Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Strong name signature not valid" (#1789)

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 10:33 AM:

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: [UWP] HttpClientHandler - Digest Authentication Broken on Windows 10 PC

Like I said, this is a new issue. The System.Net.Http.HttpClientHandler on UWP definitely did support Digest up until about a week ago.

My appxbundle was built with Target version 10.0.17134, Min version 10.0.15063.

I also tested with the latest & the problem still persists; Target version 10.0.18362, Min version 10.0.18362.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US does not affect C# compiler diagnostics for file-based apps
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: 
.NET SDK: 10.0.401
OS: Windows 10 x64

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Create project.cs:
```
Console.WriteLine("Hello");

if (false)
{
    Console.WriteLine("This produces CS0162");
}
```
2. Set the environment variable:
```
$env:DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE = "en-US"
```
3. Verify:
```
$env:DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE
dotnet --version
```
```
en-US
10.0.401
```
4. Run:
```
dotnet run .\project.cs -- r
```
5. The compiler produces localized diagnostic based on OS language (warning CS0162).


**Expected Behavior**:
With DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US, I would expect the compiler diagnostic to be displayed in English:
```
warning CS0162: Unreachable code detected
```

**Additional Observation**:
The compiler diagnostic language can be changed by adding this to the source file:
```
#:property PreferredUILang=en-US
```

This suggests that DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE is not being propagated to the C# compiler's PreferredUILang setting when compiling a file-based app.

Is this expected behavior for file-based apps, or should DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US also control the language of C# compiler diagnostics?

If it is expected behavior, is there a supported way to globally configure the C# compiler diagnostic language for file-based apps without adding #:property PreferredUILang=en-US to every source file?

I would like to add that it looks like removing ```#:property PreferredUILang=en-US``` from source file does not revert localization back to OS language.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US does not affect C# compiler diagnostics for file-based apps" (#85903)

AI-generated:

## Summary

Preserve the existing HRESULT checks in Visual Basic strong-name tests and include the actual signing-provider error text in assertion failures. This restores the `0x80131423` check in `AssemblySignatureKeyAttribute_3` and adds failure messages to both related `0x80090016` checks. The corresponding C# key-container assertions already include their error text.

This supersedes the initial proposal to remove the assertion: history shows the HRESULT identifies an invalid countersignature, independently of localized message wording. Removing it would let unrelated signing errors pass. This PR improves investigation evidence; it does **not** claim to fix the underlying flake.

## Evidence

- Investigated failure on #85776: [Azure DevOps build 1620719](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1620719)
- [Helix console log](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/06b19ee2-9ec0-4a2a-912d-5b0b4c1f9f65/workitems/workitem_18/console)
- The regular-provider case failed the HRESULT assertion while the legacy-provider case passed. Neither console nor XML results include the actual signing error, so the cause remains unconfirmed. With this change, any recurrence reports that error without weakening coverage.

## Validation

Ran `dotnet test src\Compilers\VisualBasic\Test\Emit\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Emit.UnitTests.vbproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~InternalsVisibleToAndStrongNameTests" --no-restore`:

- net472: 166 passed, 0 failed.
- net10.0: 164 passed, 1 existing skip, 0 failed.
- `dotnet format whitespace --folder . --include src\Compilers\VisualBasic\Test\Emit\Attributes\InternalsVisibleToAndStrongNameTests.vb` and `git diff --check` passed.

Validation uses main's existing test infrastructure, not #85776's xUnit v3 migration. No compiler behavior or expected test outcomes change.

Issues.Title: Add closed modifier to type in switch expression IDE diagnostic/code action
Issues.Body: ## Summary When CS8509 is shown, show an IDE suggestion to add the closed modifier to the base class and if it's defined in the same assembly. `warning CS8509: The switch expression does not handle all possible values of its input type (it is not exhaustive). For example, the pattern '_' is not covered.` ## Background and Motivation Currently when you have a switch expression in which not all cases are handled it will emit `cs8509` which suggests you add a `_`/`not null` case. This is not always useful, especially when you know your project isn't a dependency in another and you know that the cases defined are the only inheritors of the base class. ## Proposed Feature Currently the following will emit CS8509: ```cs public class BaseClass; public class Inheritor1 : BaseClass; public class Inheritor2 : BaseClass; public class Inheritor3 : BaseClass; public class C { public int M(BaseClass val) => val switch { // warning CS8509: The switch expression does not handle all possible values of its input type (it is not exhaustive). For example, the pattern 'not null' is not covered. Inheritor1 => 1, Inheritor2 => 2, Inheritor3 => 3, null => -1, }; } ``` [SharpLab for the snippet above](https://sharplab.io/#v2:) However this warning can be resolved in .net11 with the closed keyword on the type `BaseClass`, of course this isn't possible if you don't own `BaseClass`, so this would only apply if the type being switched on is defined in the same assembly. ### Full requirements for this diagnostic I will use SOT as a short hand for "Switched on type" - SOT is a class/record that can legally be closed - Without changing functionality, so it should be allowed to change an abstract class into a closed class. - This should also check if there are not instances being created of the SOT itself if the class isn't abstract - The declaration of the SOT is in an assembly that the user owns - All known direct inheritors are in the same assembly as the SOT - There are no known direct inheritors outside of the assembly of the SOT ### Conclusion So to conclude, there should be a suggested fix to add the closed modifier on the type being switched on, in this case `BaseClass`. ## Alternative Designs None, this is quite a simple feature and what it achieves can't really be achieved in another way without altering the result. Of course IDE0072 already exists but is a fundamentally different fix. If you add a default case is also bad for future proofing for when you inevitably add a new inheritor since it won't be explicitly handled which might have unforeseen consequences, adding the closed modifier to the switched on type instead will raise a nice warning instead when adding this new inheritor.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Add closed modifier to type in switch expression IDE diagnostic/code action" (#85897)

Issues.Title: Formatter inserts space in shebang ("#!" -> "# !") when indenting with tabs
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces 5.9.0-1.26357.3 (35d9211b); also .NET SDK 10.0.401 (`dotnet format`) and C# for VS Code 2.160.4

**Steps to Reproduce**:

When indenting with tabs, the C# formatter inserts a space into a file-based app's shebang line, turning `#!` into `# !`. That stops the shebang from working and also breaks the file as a file-based program. With spaces it's left alone.

Minimal repro using the formatter API (run as a file-based app with `dotnet run repro.cs`):

```csharp
#:package Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces@5.9.0-1.26357.3
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Formatting;

var root = CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText("#!/usr/bin/env dotnet\nConsole.WriteLine(1);\n").GetRoot();
var ws = new AdhocWorkspace();
foreach (var tabs in new[] { false, true })
{
    var o = ws.Options.WithChangedOption(FormattingOptions.UseTabs, LanguageNames.CSharp, tabs);
    Console.WriteLine($"UseTabs={tabs}: {Formatter.Format(root, ws, o).ToFullString().Split('\n')[0]}");
}
```

Output:

```
UseTabs=False: #!/usr/bin/env dotnet
UseTabs=True: # !/usr/bin/env dotnet
```

The same thing happens with `dotnet format` and format-on-save in VS Code when `.editorconfig` has:

```ini
root = true
[*.cs]
indent_style = tab
```

```
dotnet format whitespace --folder --include app.cs
```

where `app.cs` is:

```csharp
#!/usr/bin/env dotnet
Console.WriteLine(1);
```

Other things I checked:
- It makes no difference whether the tree is parsed with the `FileBasedProgram` feature. The leading trivia is `ShebangDirectiveTrivia` either way.
- Setting `indent_size` or `tab_width`, or `indent_size = tab`, doesn't help.
- A UTF-8 BOM, `charset = utf-8-bom` and `insert_final_newline` don't matter. `indent_style = space` alone avoids the bug.
- In VS Code the file is correctly loaded as a file-based app (`FileBasedProgramsProjectSystem` reports a successful load). The shebang is still rewritten on save.

**Expected Behavior**:

The shebang line is left unchanged (`#!/usr/bin/env dotnet`) whether indenting with tabs or spaces.

**Actual Behavior**:

With tabs, the formatter rewrites the first line to `# !/usr/bin/env dotnet`.

Workaround: use `indent_style = space` for the affected file, or save without formatting.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Formatter inserts space in shebang ("#!" -> "# !") when indenting with tabs" (#85890)

Issues.Title: RS0016 reported for Razor-generated source files despite .editorconfig exclusions
Issues.Body:
### Description

I am using `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers` in a Blazor/Razor component library. The project produces `RS0016` warnings for methods generated by the Razor source generator, especially `BuildRenderTree`.

The diagnostics point to generated files located under the `obj` directory:

```text
obj\Debug\net8.0\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.Compiler\
Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor.SourceGenerators.RazorSourceGenerator\
Components\AppBar\AppBarLogo_razor.g.cs
```

Example warning:

```text
warning RS0016:
Symbol '~override MyLib.Blazor.Components.AppBarLogo.BuildRenderTree(
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Rendering.RenderTreeBuilder __builder
) -> void' is not part of the declared public API
```

These methods are generated by Razor and are not explicitly declared in the source code.

### Environment

- .NET SDK: .net10
- Target framework: `net8.0;net9.0;net10.0`
- Project type: Blazor/Razor component library
- IDE: Visual Studio 18.9.2
- OS: Windows
- Package: `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers`
- Package version: `5.6.0`

### Package reference

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers"
                  Version="5.*"
                  PrivateAssets="all">
  <IncludeAssets>
    runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers; buildtransitive
  </IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

### Current `.editorconfig`

```ini
root = true

[**/*.g.cs]
generated_code = true
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0016.severity = none
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0041.severity = none
```

I also tried the following patterns:

```ini
[**/*_razor.g.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0016.severity = none
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0041.severity = none

[**/obj/**/*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0016.severity = none
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0041.severity = none
```

However, the `RS0016` warnings are still reported.

### `.globalconfig`

```ini
is_global = true

dotnet_diagnostic.RS0041.severity = none
```

Adding `RS0016` globally suppresses the warning:

```ini
dotnet_diagnostic.RS0016.severity = none
```

However, this disables the rule for the entire project/solution, including handwritten source code. I would prefer to keep `RS0016` enabled for manually written public APIs and exclude only generated Razor code.

### Additional test

I also tried the following MSBuild property:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <SuppressRazorSourceGeneratorDiagnostics>true</SuppressRazorSourceGeneratorDiagnostics>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This does not suppress the `RS0016` warnings.

### Expected behavior

I would expect one of the following solutions to work:

1. `RS0016` can be disabled for Razor-generated files using `.editorconfig`;
2. generated files under `obj` are automatically ignored by `PublicApiAnalyzers`;
3. there is an analyzer-specific configuration option to exclude source-generated files;
4. there is a supported MSBuild property to prevent `PublicApiAnalyzers` from analyzing Razor-generated symbols.

### Actual behavior

`RS0016` is reported for generated Razor methods such as:

```text
BuildRenderTree(RenderTreeBuilder __builder)
```

The diagnostic is associated with a generated `.g.cs` file under `obj`, but file-based `.editorconfig` exclusions do not appear to be applied.

### Questions

- Does `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers` support excluding source-generated files?
- Are `.editorconfig` file patterns expected to apply to diagnostics reported on symbols originating from source generators?

- Is this a known issue or limitation of `RS0016`?
- Should generated Razor components be explicitly excluded from Public API analysis?

Any guidance or workaround would be appreciated.

Issues.Title: Prevent odd document Uris from causing inadvertent syntax errors
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/issues/9831

For the left hand side of a diff, VS Code will create documents with Uris like `git://filename.razor?{"path":"filename.razor"}`, and the quotes (and other things) can end up causing syntax errors due to them incorrectly terminating line directives, and at the same time our file kind detection can end up seeing the `.razor?` and falling back to the legacy (cshtml) file kind, which then can cause other errors because the directive set is different.

This fixes both by encoding file paths as appropriate for generated C#, and using a method we already had to find the "real" file path from a Uri in a few more places.

Issues.Title: [ResourceLock] Lock workload-resolver opt-out env var across MSBuildSdkResolver tests
Issues.Body:
**Project:** `test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests` — `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel` (already parallelized; this PR does not change it).

**Shared resource:** process environment variable `MSBuildEnableWorkloadResolver`.
- Mutators: `GivenACachingWorkloadResolver.WithOptOut` (set/restore in `finally`), used by 5 tests.
- Concurrent observers: `GivenAnMSBuildSdkResolver` tests call `DotNetMSBuildSdkResolver.Resolve`, which constructs `CachingWorkloadResolver` and calls `IsEnabled()`, reading that variable (`src/Resolvers/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadMSBuildSdkResolver/CachingWorkloadResolver.cs`). Under ClassLevel parallelism a resolve test could observe `false` and skip workload resolution.

**Change:** `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` on the 5 env-mutating methods only (the other tests in that class do not touch the variable), and on `GivenAnMSBuildSdkResolver` at class level since every `Resolve` call there samples the variable. Previous values were already restored exactly in `finally`.

**Validation**
- `./.dotnet/dotnet build test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests.csproj` — succeeded, 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- `./.dotnet/dotnet scripts/RunTests.cs -- --skip-redist-check --project test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests.csproj` — **not run to completion**: the project targets only `net472`, and the runner reports it "can only run on Windows". `--framework net11.0` fails with NETSDK1005. Tests were not executed on this Linux runner.

Issues.Title: [ResourceLock] Use ResourceLock instead of DoNotParallelize in NuGetPackageDownloaderFactoryTests
Issues.Body:
Replaces `[DoNotParallelize]` with a method-level `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` in `Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests`, and adds the matching lock to the one test that observes the same variable.

**Project / scope:** `test/Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests`, `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel`.

**Shared resource and conflicting tests:** `DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION`. The `NuGetPackageDownloader` constructor reads it when `verifySignatures` is true (`src/Cli/dotnet/NugetPackageDownloader/NuGetPackageDownloader.cs`).
- `Constructor_WhenVerifyRequestedButPlatformUnsupported_LogsMessage` mutates it (restored in `finally`).

- Other constructions in the project pass `verifySignatures: false`, which short-circuits before the read, so they need no lock.

**Why minimal:** the variable lives in this assembly, so the in-assembly lock covers both the mutator and the observer. Both locks are method-level; the rest of the class stays fully parallel.

Issues.Title: Normalize package pseudo-locale satellite casing consistently
Issues.Body:
🤖 Windows NLS and ICU disagree on the casing of pseudo-locale names, leaving package satellite output directories and NETSDK1187 diagnostics dependent on the build host. This addresses the remaining casing issue in #53815 while preserving the culture-remapping protection introduced by merged PR #53817.

## Approach

- Recognize only `qps-ploc`, `qps-plocm`, and `qps-ploca`, case-insensitively, and use lowercase output culture/destination metadata without casing diagnostics.
- Preserve original package paths, satellite assembly culture metadata, and embedded resource names. Ordinary corrections such as `ru-ru` to `ru-RU` and the protection against NLS remapping `ckb` to `ku` remain unchanged.
- Increment the asset cache version so existing caches cannot retain the old normalization results.
- Add regressions for casing variants, language filtering, warm/old caches, build/publish output, `.deps.json`, unchanged satellite bytes/metadata, and actual NLS/ICU resource loading without parent fallback.

## Validation

- Repository build succeeded.
- ResolvePackageAssets task tests: 61 passed.
- Satellite culture integration tests: 18 passed, including the existing Kurdish regressions.
- Focused ILLink publishing tests: 4 passed.
- Prior compatibility investigation also verified Linux ICU loading on a case-sensitive filesystem using SDK 10.0.401/runtime 10.0.12. The patched SDK regression run was on Windows; macOS was not executed.

Fixes #53815

Fixes: #53817

Issues.Title: Expand optimized publish to conservative trimmed app scenarios
Issues.Body:
🤖 Extend `UseOptimizedPublish` beyond Native AOT so eligible trimmed applications avoid a redundant root-project build deployment while still compiling. This is the first conservative .NET 12 rollout, not a general replacement for Build during publish.

## Approach

- Default to optimized publish for plain trimmed, self-contained C# executables targeting net11+ on an explicit desktop/server RID allowlist. Eligibility is separate from the public switch, so explicit `true` cannot force unsupported scenarios.
- Keep combined single-file/ReadyToRun modes, specialized SDKs/workloads, native-interoperability scenarios, and older TFMs outside the new expansion. Existing Native AOT eligibility remains unchanged.
- Generate managed runtime configuration under the intermediate publish directory using shared runtime-setting preparation, without rebasing public build paths. Collect XML documentation from compiler output and keep dependency metadata publish-owned.
- Preserve `UseOptimizedPublish=false`, the separate NoBuild route, explicit Build, and normal project-reference builds. Register the intermediate runtime configuration for Clean without priming Build's incremental-clean snapshot or enrolling the published deployment in its ownership.

The TFM policy deliberately includes net11 projects using SDK 12; it is not net12-only. Build-hook integrations that need runnable `bin` output must opt out until adapted. The documentation describes this behavior change and OpenAPI/XML serializer coordination limitations.

## Validation

- Redist build succeeded with zero warnings or errors.
- 52 focused trimmed-publish/ILLink cases passed, covering runnable trimmed output, resources/content, opt-out, unsupported eligibility, NoBuild, repeated publish, custom paths, Build/Publish ordering, and Clean behavior.
- Four existing Native AOT and unsupported-mode controls passed, including executable project-reference coverage.
- No skipped cases. Local execution was Windows x64; other allowlisted platforms still require CI validation.

Related to #55911; this implements only the first rollout step.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Add incremental container archive publishing
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Backports [#55850](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55850) to `release/11.0.2xx`, faithfully porting the final merged behavior and regression tests from merge commit `371eae68d4d0c9cbbfc2e04d6cc56e81f61ae0c6` (final PR head `209f94e639d06c43ade49fe5b49ace487dd9dedd`).

Release-specific adaptations:
- Add the new public APIs to the `net11.0` baseline instead of `net12.0`.
- Preserve the release branch's existing file-mode semantics while extracting the shared helper; do not import the unrelated permission calculation change from main.

Includes incremental single-platform archive reuse, the opt-out property, cached task outputs, archive integrity verification, atomic archive replacement, timestamp validation, and the source regression tests and resource updates.

Release base: `c9b7ae4a99ee9b8bf0d07c688921761d2a9aeea8`.

## Validation

- Full isolated SDK build passed (`build.cmd /bl:1.binlog`).
- Focused `CreateNewImageTests` and `ContainerArchiveTests`: 57 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- TRX and unique build binlogs retained locally.

Issues.Title: Remove Mono packs from .NET 12 workloads
Issues.Body:
## Description

This PR removes .NET 12 Mono runtime and cross-AOT pack references from SDK resolution, current workloads, and Windows workload acquisition so they do not request the removed packs. It does not add CoreCLR runtime packs to the workloads, since the SDK resolves them through `KnownFrameworkReference`, and it removes the `_DisableCheckForUnsupportedMonoMobileRuntime` bypass. It adds `net11` versioned Mono toolchain and Emscripten manifests pinned to the .NET 11 packs, so `net11.0` browser and mobile projects keep resolving their Mono workload packs, and the Helix AoT tests install `wasm-tools-net11` because their test apps target `net11.0`. Existing versioned manifests remain unchanged.

Contributes to dotnet/runtime#134397.

> [!NOTE]
> Prepared with GitHub Copilot.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Remove Mono packs from .NET 12 workloads" (#56480)

Issues.Title: NativeAOT for Android and iOS is using the wrong ILC and runtime pack
Issues.Body:
I installed .NET 11 RC1, then try using NativeAOT in my MAUI apps to publish for Android and iOS. 

But it tries to use the version that is not on the public nuget.org, instead it uses the one in the .NET 11 nightly azdo nuget feed, which causes the restoration to fail due to ilc and runtime pack package not found.

Issues.Title: `dotnet watch` drops an existing `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS` (from the environment or the launch profile) instead of composing with it
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When an app already has a startup hook in `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, whether from the parent environment or from the launch profile's `environmentVariables`, `dotnet watch` silently drops it. The app runs with only the Hot Reload agent's hook. A tool that relies on a startup hook (an APM or tracing agent, a test helper, a diagnostics tool) stops working under `dotnet watch` and gives no indication why.

The composition code clearly means to keep existing hooks. `DefaultHotReloadClient.ConfigureLaunchEnvironment` calls `environmentBuilder.InsertListItem(DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS, startupHookPath, Path.PathSeparator)`, and `HotReloadAgent.ClearHotReloadEnvironmentVariables` later removes only its own entry. But in `ProjectLauncher.TryLaunchProcessAsync` the `environmentBuilder` starts empty for the main project. `GetMainProjectOptions` sets `LaunchEnvironmentVariables = []`, and on `main` the seeding loop is gone entirely. So `InsertListItem` never sees an existing value, and the result is passed as `dotnet run … -e DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS=<agent>`, which overrides both the inherited value and the launch profile's.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A startup hook library, `Hook`:

   ```csharp
   internal class StartupHook
   {
       public static void Initialize()
       {
           var entry = System.Reflection.Assembly.GetEntryAssembly()?.GetName().Name;
           System.Console.WriteLine($"[hook] my startup hook ran in '{entry}'");
       }
   }
   ```

2. A console app, `App`:

   ```csharp
   Console.WriteLine("[app] STARTUP_HOOKS=" + (AppContext.GetData("STARTUP_HOOKS") as string ?? "<unset>"));
   Thread.Sleep(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
   ```

   with `Properties/launchSettings.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "profiles": {
       "NoHook":   { "commandName": "Project" },
       "WithHook": { "commandName": "Project", "environmentVariables": { "DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS": "/abs/path/Hook.dll" } }
     }
   }
   ```

3. Build both, then run from `App/`:

   ```bash
   DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS=/abs/path/Hook.dll dotnet run --launch-profile NoHook          # control 1
   dotnet run --launch-profile WithHook                                                # control 2
   DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS=/abs/path/Hook.dll dotnet watch --non-interactive run --launch-profile NoHook
   dotnet watch --non-interactive run --launch-profile WithHook
   ```

### Expected behavior

Under `dotnet watch`, the app's startup hooks are the Hot Reload agent **plus** the existing hook (`<agent>:<Hook.dll>`), and `[hook] … ran in 'App'` is printed, as it is under `dotnet run`.

### Actual behavior

| Command | Hook ran in `App`? | App's effective `STARTUP_HOOKS` |
|---|---|---|
| `dotnet run`, hook in the parent environment | yes | `…/Hook.dll` |
| `dotnet run`, hook in the launch profile | yes | `…/Hook.dll` |
| `dotnet watch run`, hook in the parent environment | **no** | `…/dotnet-watch/…/hotreload/net10.0/Microsoft.Extensions.DotNetDeltaApplier.dll` only |
| `dotnet watch run`, hook in the launch profile | **no** | `…/Microsoft.Extensions.DotNetDeltaApplier.dll` only |

The results are identical on SDK 10.0.301 and on SDK 11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103 (runtime 10.0.12, linux-x64). With the hook in the parent environment it does run, but only in the `dotnet` and `dotnet-watch` processes, never in the app.

**Workaround.** Declaring the hook in the app's runtimeconfig survives, because the host combines the runtime property with the environment value. The app's effective list is then `<agent>:<Hook.dll>`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="STARTUP_HOOKS" Value="/abs/path/Hook.dll" />
</ItemGroup>
```

That needs a change to the app's project file, which an external tool usually cannot make.

### Suggested fix

Before `ConfigureLaunchEnvironment`, seed `environmentBuilder[DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS]` with the value the app would otherwise have received: the selected launch profile's `environmentVariables` entry if there is one, otherwise the value inherited from `dotnet watch`'s own environment. `InsertListItem` then produces `<agent><sep><existing>` as intended. A test could assert that a pre-existing hook survives for both sources.

### Exact versions

- .NET SDK 10.0.301 and 11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103; runtime 10.0.12
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, x64

Issues.Title: [AI discovered CI] dotnet.Tests.dll.18 aborts with core dump on Linux Helix
Issues.Body:
## Build Information

- **Current build:** [dotnet-sdk-public-ci 20261001.9](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1619854)
- **Branch:** `refs/heads/main` (`ff7814cdd3096e3a9b06c0a37d1d2638733ae892`)
- **Failing work item:** `dotnet.Tests.dll.18` in `Linux x64 - ubuntu.2204.amd64.open`
- **Phase:** `test-execution`
- **Failure type:** `process-crash`
- **Evidence sources:** `helix-console`, `process-exit-code`, `helix-trx`
- **Failure fingerprint:** `test-execution|process-crash|dotnet.tests.dll.<n>|aborted-core-dumped-export-_commandexitcode-<n>-xargs--<n>--i-cp-datadisks-disk1-work-c3670a09-w-ae6d094e-uploads-find-datadisks-disk1-work-c3670a09-w-ae6d094e-uploads-..-..-..--na`
- **Matching prior builds:** none identified in the supplied evidence. The related failures in builds [1619713](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1619713), [1618484](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1618484), [1618022](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1618022), [1617646](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1617646), and [1617544](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1617544) show materially different test mechanisms and are not counted as matching occurrences.

## Failure History

The matching occurrence count is **1**: the current build only. The surrounding pipeline sequence was failed (`1619713`), passed (`1618837`), then failed (`1619854`), but the supplied evidence does not establish that the earlier failures had the same crash cause. This is an observed recurrence pattern for the pipeline, not evidence that this specific crash is recurring.

## Error Details

The work item reported `Aborted (core dumped)`, exported `_commandExitCode=134`, and exited with code 134 after 173 of 190 tests passed. The console reported signal 6 while `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.IPC.NamedPipeServer.<WaitConnectionAsync>b__27_0()` was active, then successfully wrote a crash report and a 290,549,760-byte full dump.

- [Helix console log](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/ffc5ecef-0c08-4eb5-9059-f21f0b18ac76/workitems/dotnet.Tests.dll.18/files/console.0040a3c4.log?api-version=2019-06-17)
- [TRX result](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/ffc5ecef-0c08-4eb5-905f21f0b18ac76/workitems/dotnet.Tests.dll.18/files/dotnet.Tests_net12.0_x64.trx?api-version=2019-06-17)

The supplied artifact list does not include a downloadable dump URL; it only records the dump path in the console evidence.

## Root Cause Analysis

- **Observed:** The `dotnet.Tests.dll.18` process terminated with SIGABRT/exit 134 during test execution. The crash occurred while the testing platform was waiting on its named-pipe server, and Helix captured a core dump.
- **Assessment:** This is an SDK test-execution process crash, not a test assertion or the downstream `Monitor Helix Jobs` task itself. The evidence establishes the proximate process abort but does not establish whether the trigger is a test-host/runtime defect, an IPC failure, or an environment-specific condition.
- **Confidence:** **Medium** for the process-crash characterization; **Low** for the underlying cause.
- **Alternatives / Unknowns:** No dump analysis, stack trace, target-branch comparison, or source/change correlation is present. The crash may be isolated to this work-item environment, or may reflect a repeatable test-platform/IPC failure; the supplied evidence cannot distinguish these.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Analyze the captured core dump and crash-report JSON for the crashing thread's native and managed stack, especially around the testing-platform named-pipe server.
2. Compare the same `dotnet.Tests.dll.18` shard across the next build and a known-good Linux run to determine whether the crash reproduces on the same test set.
3. If reproducible, inspect the affected test-host/IPC path and correlate the crash with the shard's final test and the tested SDK tree; otherwise route as an environment-specific Helix incident.

The generic `Monitor Helix Jobs` failure is a downstream summary of the failed work item, not the root cause.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.2xx] Backport Microsoft-internal CLI telemetry classification
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Backport of #56388 to `release/11.0.2xx`.

- add the AOT-compatible `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.InternalMicrosoft` detection library and staged providers
- enrich normal CLI telemetry activities from one cached classification result
- preserve the privacy, cancellation, timeout, cache, and CI behavior from the original change
- include the section-aware `dsregcmd` parsing hardening for hybrid and multiple-tenant machines
- retain managed CLI, Native AOT CLI, and MSBuild logger integration

The release-only `Program.cs` conflict was resolved by preserving this branch's existing shutdown lifecycle and adding only the bounded internal-detection wait before the main activity stops. Repository memory files from `main` were not brought into the release branch because they do not exist there.

## Aspire prior art

As in #56388, this is based on Aspire CLI's staged internal-user detection and asynchronous tag enrichment:

- [`InternalMicrosoftDetector`](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/blob/bcdcd4b05edb39210c634101d030404ec18a0a7b/src/Aspire.Cli/Telemetry/InternalMicrosoftDetector.cs)

## Validation

- detector library build: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors
- Native AOT CLI build: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors

- `InternalMicrosoftDetectorTests`: 31 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

Issues.Title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 1
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31
